Zod schemas' toString() yields '[object Object]', so both computed keys collide (second overwrites first) and the object effectively only validates access_token; Zod strips unknown keys, so expiry and other token fields would be silently dropped when credential sharing is enabled. judged_text: The computed-key schema produces only the literal key "[object Object]" (both `z.string().toString()` and `z.string().optional().toString()` evaluate to the same string, and the second overwrites the first), so minimumTokenResponseSchema accepts only {access_token} and the comment's 'any property with a number is the expiry' is not implemented. When credential-sharing is enabled, every refreshed-token payload parsed by this schema is stripped to {access_token} (Zod strips unknown keys), so expiry and all other token fields are silently dropped, and callers persist a near-empty credential to the DB.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. These evaluate to a single fixed string key (not a wildcard), and since both expressions produce the same key, the second definition overwrites the first in the object literal. As a result, the schema does not implement “any property with a number is the expiry” and will only reliably parse/retain `access_token` (and possibly that one literal key), while Zod’s default object behavior strips unknown keys. When credential sharing is enabled, callers using `parseRefreshTokenResponse` will therefore drop `expiry_date`/`expires_in` and other token fields from parsed data, matching the finding’s described behavior.
